bounds.domain: One provider key, three one-shot callers and up to three executions. Two callers have cancellation signals. The second case allows a one-off caller. Promise settlement and cleanup are separate.
bounds.limitations: The real state-composition suite checks coalescing, isolation, cancellation, eviction, shutdown and provider failures. Provider payloads, cache keys and provider streaming and tracing are outside the finite execution model.

stateRepresentation: The source variables form one typed record. Every action updates that record atomically and retains all other fields.

assumptions: Checked formula in ProviderExecution: DeadlockFree = always(enabled(nextStep))
No scheduler fairness is assumed by this property.
Checked formula in ProviderExecution: AbortedCallerLeaves = Fairness.implies(Callers.forall(c => (s.pc.get(c) == "attached" and s.cause.get(s.exec.get(c)) != "none").leadsTo(s.pc.get(c) == "done")))
Model fairness predicate Fairness = and { Execs.forall(e => SettleAborted(e).weakFair(s) and Cleanup(e).weakFair(s)), Callers.forall(c => CallerSettle(c).weakFair(s)), StopComposer.weakFair(s) }
The stated fairness is an assumption about enabled model actions; runtime scheduling and provider completion are not proved.
Checked formula in ProviderExecution: StopReleasesCallers = Fairness.implies(Callers.forall(c => (s.pc.get(c) == "attached" and s.stopped).leadsTo(s.pc.get(c) == "done")))
Model fairness predicate Fairness = and { Execs.forall(e => SettleAborted(e).weakFair(s) and Cleanup(e).weakFair(s)), Callers.forall(c => CallerSettle(c).weakFair(s)), StopComposer.weakFair(s) }
The stated fairness is an assumption about enabled model actions; runtime scheduling and provider completion are not proved.
Cleanup and caller settlement callbacks are weakly fair once enabled.
Provider work is not assumed to settle on its own.
